## Why I'm speaking today

- One issue only: **How fast total compensation is growing**
- This is about **math and sustainability**, not politics
- If recurring costs grow faster than stable revenue, tax rate pressure builds

---

## FY25 baseline (from City payroll spreadsheet)

- Estimated **General-Fund-type** total compensation: **~$35.0M**
- Benefits are a major driver:
  - Benefits are about **39% of earnings**
  - Fully-loaded compensation rises even when wages are flat

---

## FY26 merit/step cost is shown as midyear

The budget states:

> “These changes are planned to take effect midyear and cost $784,000.”

So the **full-year wage impact** is:

- $784k × 2 = **$1.568M/year**

With the FY25 benefits load applied, the **fully-loaded recurring impact** is about:

- **~$2.18M/year**

---

## What “doubling time” means

If total compensation grows at a steady annual rate, it eventually doubles.

- Faster growth = **much faster doubling**
- Doubling means the City needs **much more revenue** just to keep services the same

---

## Sensitivity: years to double at different growth rates

| Annual growth rate | Approx. years to double |
|---:|---:|
| 3% | 24 |
| 4% | 18 |
| 5% | 14 |
| 6% | 12 |
| 7% | 10 |

**Important caveat:** Even if no additional raises are approved, total compensation can still grow **3–5%** due to benefits (healthcare, retirement, payroll taxes). A one-year medical plan “no increase” does not remove long-term inflation.

---

## The warning bell

- A recurring fully-loaded increase of roughly **$2.18M/year** is not a one-time event  
- It becomes part of the payroll base and compounds
- That pushes the City toward a **12–16 year** doubling-time zone under realistic assumptions

---

## The financial principle (must say)

A fundamental financial principle is:

- **Match long-term commitments with long-term reliable revenue**

Recurring compensation is a **long-term commitment**.

Temporary conditions (one-year insurance freezes, unusually strong sales tax months, short-term workarounds) are **not** long-term funding.

If the curves do not match, **dramatic tax rate increases are not optional — they become inevitable**.

---

## Closing

- I support fair pay and retaining staff
- My concern is the **long-run math**
- Please treat the doubling-time signal as an early warning, and plan accordingly

Thank you.
